learn.title: From idea to code
learn.body: Two integers mark what is still possible: `lo` is the first index in play and `hi` is the last. The loop keeps going while `lo <= hi`. When `lo` passes `hi` nothing is left, and we return -1.

learn.title: The function
learn.body: Each round we pick the middle `mid`, compare, and move one end past `mid`.

learn.title: Why lo + (hi - lo) / 2
learn.body: The middle could be written `(lo + hi) / 2`. For huge arrays `lo + hi` can overflow an int, which is a bug. Writing `lo + (hi - lo) / 2` gives the same middle and never overflows. With `lo` 0 and `hi` 6 it gives 3.

learn.title: Why mid + 1 and mid - 1
learn.body: We already compared `a[mid]` and it was not the target. So `mid` itself can be removed. Setting `lo = mid` instead could loop forever when `lo` and `hi` are next to each other.

learn.title: Trace: target 4 in {1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13}
steps: Now `lo` 2 is greater than `hi` 1, so return -1

questions.explanation: 11 is stored at index 5. The function returns the index, not the value.

questions.prompt: What does `binary(s, 7, 4)` return for the same array?
questions.explanation: 4 is not in the array, so the ends cross and the function returns -1.

questions.prompt: When does the `while (lo <= hi)` loop stop with no match?
choices: When `a[mid]` is bigger than the target
questions.explanation: Then no index is left to check.

questions.prompt: If `a[mid] < t`, the target must be to the right, so we set \_\_.
questions.explanation: Everything up to and including `mid` is too small, so the low end moves past it.
6 - 0 is 6, 6 / 2 is 3, and 0 + 3 is 3. Integer division drops any fraction.

questions.prompt: Why write `lo + (hi - lo) / 2` instead of `(lo + hi) / 2`?
choices: It can not overflow for huge arrays
questions.explanation: Both give the same middle, but adding two large indexes can overflow an int.

questions.prompt: Put these lines of one loop round in order.
questions.explanation: Find the middle, test it, shrink the range, then test whether anything is left.
